question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Nvidia)

calls.reasoning: Nvidia guided Q3 FY27 (quarter ended Oct 25, 2026) to $108B ±2%, with zero China data-center compute assumed. Results come Nov 17, 2026, so nothing is resolved yet. Over the last 7 quarters actual revenue beat the guidance midpoint by 2.5–8%, median ~5%. Two examples: Q2 FY27 came in at 96.2 vs a 91 guide (+5.7%), and Q4 FY26 at 68.1 vs 65 (+4.8%). Applying those beats to 108 gives a median near $113B. Some analysts project $113–114B. The aggregator consensus of $108.8B sits close to the guide, as it usually does. The upside tail above $116B would take a beat above 7.4%, which happened about once in 7 quarters. Vera Rubin's ramp (~20% of data-center revenue) and the supply commitments support upside. Supply limits or ramp hiccups could cap the beat. Markets: no Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi contract on the revenue figure found.

- Q2 FY27 actual: $96.22B against a $91.0B ±2% guide, a +5.7% beat on the midpoint. Data center was $89B (SEC 8-K q2fy27pr; cryptobriefing).
- Earlier quarters, actual vs guide midpoint: Q1 FY27 81.6 vs ~78 (~+4.6%); Q4 FY26 68.1 vs 65 (+4.8%); Q3 FY26 57.0 vs 54 (+5.6%); Q2 FY26 46.7 vs 45 (+3.9%); Q1 FY26 44.1 vs 43 (+2.5%, H20 export hit); Q3 FY25 35.1 vs 32.5 (+7.9%). The last 4 come from my background knowledge of past releases.
- Vera Rubin production shipments began in August 2026; management expects it to be ~20% of Q3 data-center revenue.
- Long-term supply/capacity commitments were $279B as of July 2026, up from $119B the quarter before (cryptobriefing/Seeking Alpha preview).
- Consensus: MarketBeat shows $108.8B. Some analyst projections are $113–114B (cryptobriefing).
- Earnings date: Tue Nov 17, 2026, release ~1:20pm PT (Nvidia IR / Investing.com). The quarter ended Oct 25, 2026.
- Status quo: Nvidia has beaten its midpoint every quarter for years.
- Resolves off the total revenue in Nvidia's Q3 FY27 8-K press release, not data-center revenue or any later revision.
- Event window: the first quarterly release after Sep 30, 2026 → the Nov 17, 2026 release. As of Nov 8 it has not been reported.
- Searched without finding: a Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold revenue contract; any preannouncement.

calls.reasoning: Nvidia guided Q3 FY2027 revenue to $108B +/-2% (Aug 26, 2026), excluding China DC compute. It has beaten the top of its guidance range 12 straight quarters, averaging ~3.1% above the high end over the last four, and recent quarters beat the midpoint by ~4.6-5.7% (Q1 FY27 $78B guide -> $81.6B; Q2 $96.2B actual). That centers the outcome around $113-114B. Topping $116B needs a ~7.4% beat; that's plausible with China resuming or a supply ramp, priced at ~10%. Falling below $105B would be a first guidance miss in years, ~1%. No Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmaker market found.

calls.reasoning: Guide $108B ±2% (ex-China DC). Over the last 8 quarters Nvidia beat its guide midpoint by +2.5% to +7.9%, median ~+5%, with no misses; applied to $108B that centers near $113B. q/q growth in line with recent ~18% gives ~$113.5B. The Vera Rubin ramp and previews at $113-114B support this; higher-than-expected memory costs and supply limits cap the beat. >$116B needs a >7.4% beat (1 of 8 quarters, plus a China-resumption path): ~10%. <$105B would be the first guide miss in years: ~1%. calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the guide ($108B ±2%), the beat history and the median (~$113.1B). Factual disputes: (1) Earnings date, Nov 17 vs Nov 25: unresolvable without web access, but irrelevant because either is the first release after Sep 30. (2) Consensus $103.88B vs $108.8B: the $103.88B figure sits below the guidance floor, so it is likely stale; I discounted it. Judgment: tail masses (8-10% above $116B, 0-1% below $105B). I took 10%/1% given the 1-in-8 frequency of beats >7.4% plus China upside, and no precedent for a midpoint miss in the window. I carried the runs' reference class forward and widened dispersion slightly to match the SD of beat sizes.
